title: driver-sql: on PostgreSQL, a schema sync that adds an index to an existing large table builds it CONCURRENTLY, so writes are not locked during the build (follow-up of #31882)
body:
domain:server#3 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQXLfvyB5R53VDm3Ka

Filing gate: ④ coordination node: seat answer 6738355121 on #31882 (item 4). #31882 adds implicit indexes through the same plain `CREATE INDEX` path declared indexes take at schema sync. On PostgreSQL that holds a write lock on the table for the length of the build (543 ms measured at 1M rows; longer on larger tables). ⛔ Not a claim.
Business reason: the first boot after an upgrade on a large hosted tenant blocks writes to the indexed tables while each index builds.
Reader: the `domain:server` seat, after #31882 lands.
Dedupe (open AND closed): `create index concurrently postgres schema sync` → none on point.
class: c · type: Feature
Blocked-by: #31882

## 维护者速读

升级后第一次启动时，PostgreSQL 上给已有大表补建索引会短暂锁住写入。这张卡改成并发建索引，不锁写入。

## What to build

- On PostgreSQL, the schema sync's additive `create_index` for an existing table uses `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` (outside a transaction, as PostgreSQL requires). A build that fails leaves an INVALID index, so the next sync detects it, drops it and retries. Other dialects keep their current path.
- Pins: a write during the build is not blocked (PG); a failed concurrent build is cleaned up and rebuilt on the next sync; a second sync is a no-op.
- Clause-②: no. Metadata-protocol: none.
